entry.title: Custom runner labels at repo level for Dependabot [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now target specific self-hosted runners for Dependabot jobs at the repository level, giving you finer control over where dependency update workflows run. This complements existing org-level runner configuration, so teams managing large enterprises can tailor runner selection to individual repositories without affecting the broader organization. Whether you need a runner with particular network access, hardware specs, or compliance requirements, Dependabot jobs will now respect the labels you define.

Expected Outcome

Enterprise teams gain a more flexible, granular way to configure Dependabot across their GitHub environment, reducing friction when rolling out dependency automation at scale. By supporting custom runner labels at the repository level, organizations can enforce consistent infrastructure requirements for Dependabot-generated pull requests without resorting to workarounds. This makes it easier to manage Dependabot in complex, security-conscious environments where runner placement matters.

entry.title: New dashboard experience follow-up work [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The dashboard now shows more of your pull requests and issues at once while keeping titles readable and results scannable. Reduced padding means you can see more work that matters without extra clicks or navigation, and improved filtering for Agent sessions helps you find the sessions you actually need.

Expected Outcome

We're making the GitHub dashboard more efficient so developers can quickly scan and act on their work. By showing six pull requests and issues by default instead of three, reducing visual clutter, and improving session filtering, we're helping teams spend less time navigating and more time shipping.

entry.title: User owned issue fields and issue types [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Issue types and issue fields are now available in your personal repositories, giving you the same structured planning capabilities that teams in organizations have been using to standardize their workflows. You can customize issue types and fields to match how you work, making it easier to organize and track your projects with consistency.

Expected Outcome

By extending issue types and issue fields to user-owned repositories, we're empowering individual developers to bring enterprise-grade planning tools to their personal projects. This makes GitHub a unified platform for planning at any scale—from solo projects to large team efforts—and helps users develop better practices around how they organize and track their work.

entry.title: GitHub Actions will block `pull_request_target` by default in affected public repositories [Closing Down]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Actions automatically blocks the risky pull_request_target trigger in public repositories by default, protecting your secrets and build pipeline from potential exploits. You keep full control—explicitly allow the trigger in your Actions policies whenever your workflows specifically need it.

Expected Outcome

Public repositories will have safer default settings for GitHub Actions workflows. This change reduces the risk of attackers stealing repository secrets or compromising the build pipeline by executing untrusted code from pull requests, while still allowing teams to enable the trigger when they have a legitimate need.

entry.title: GitHub Copilot CLI/App - Computer Use [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub Copilot can now interact directly with desktop applications on your machine — reading what's on screen, clicking buttons, filling in fields, and navigating workflows — so you can automate tasks that go beyond code and terminals. This is especially powerful for working with legacy or GUI-only software where no API or integration exists. You stay in control throughout, with runtime permission checks that keep automation guarded and transparent.

Expected Outcome

Developers and enterprises spend significant time on repetitive, manual desktop workflows that are difficult to script or integrate. By giving Copilot the ability to drive any application through natural language prompts, teams can automate a much wider range of tasks without writing custom tooling. The goal is to expand what Copilot can do for you — from a coding assistant to a capable agent that works across your entire desktop environment.

entry.title: Planning tab for organizations and users [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The Planning tab gives organizations and users a single, consistent place to find and organize work across all their repositories. Instead of jumping between project URLs and individual repos, you can open issues and access projects from one unified view scoped to your account. This makes it easier for teams to get a clear picture of work in flight and plan across the full breadth of their account.

Expected Outcome

Teams spend less time hunting for context and more time doing meaningful work. By surfacing a dedicated planning home at the organization and user level, this feature helps teams build consistent planning habits and reduces the friction of coordinating work across repositories. The result is a clearer, faster path from identifying work to organizing and acting on it.

entry.title: Enterprise Managed Authorization (ID-JAG, XAA) allows apps to silently SSO into GitHub using corporate credentials [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Enterprise Managed Authorization (EMA, also known as ID-JAG or Cross-app access) lets you use your corporate identity in compatible apps to access GitHub without completing a separate sign-in or OAuth consent flow. When you use your corporate credentials to sign in to VS Code, Claude, or another app that supports EMA, you'll have immediate access to GitHub - no JSON or extra logins required.

EMA is a rare overlap of security and usability - identity administrators can better enforce their existing IdP access policies and get more detailed audit logs while developers get a faster, easier way to connect their tools to GitHub.

Expected Outcome

This public preview is targeted at Enterprise Managed Users, whose identity is already owned by a corporate IdP. Client apps that support EMA, in conjunction with compatible IdPs such as Entra, Okta, or Ping, will be able to access GitHub on behalf of an EMU user without an additional sign in flow. When the user signs into the app using their corporate IdP credentials, they will be able to immediately start using GitHub.

entry.title: Issues Board View [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now visualize and prioritize your work on a board without leaving issues behind. The issues board view lets teams organize, triage, and update work using a flexible, query-driven layout while keeping the issue as the single source of truth. There's no need to duplicate effort across separate planning tools — your board and your issues stay in sync automatically.

Expected Outcome

Teams that plan visually can now do so entirely within GitHub, eliminating the fragmentation that comes from managing work across issues and disconnected project boards. By bringing board-style planning directly into the issues experience, teams spend less time reconciling competing records and more time shipping. This public preview gives teams an early look at a more unified planning workflow and invites feedback to shape the final experience.

entry.title: Granular issue status [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

GitHub issues now support granular workflow statuses — like "Backlog," "Todo," or "In Progress" — that go beyond the basic open and closed states. Teams can track exactly where work stands across issue lists, boards, APIs, and automation without needing to stitch together labels and project fields. This gives everyone a single, consistent view of work status, from teammates to automated agents.

Expected Outcome

Teams spend less time maintaining workarounds and more time shipping, with a shared understanding of issue state that works everywhere GitHub does. By surfacing durable, structured status natively in issues, teams can report on progress accurately, automate workflows reliably, and keep projects moving without ambiguity.

entry.title: Modern PR experience :: Overview and improved navigation [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

The new pull request experience improves velocity by helping users, regardless of their role, focus on what matters most and take action with confidence. This new experience introduces an improved landing page that puts merge status and comments front and center, and summarizes what's new so users can quickly jump back in. Improved navigation brings information closer and reduces tab switching.

Expected Outcome

By providing a tailored overview that surfaces key information and findings, we aim to help reviewers and contributors save time and reduce context switching. This release should lead to quicker, more informed reviews and smoother collaboration across teams.

entry.title: Show repo member role labels in Issue list view [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Repository maintainers can now see role labels—such as Owner, Member, Collaborator, Contributor, First-time contributor, and First-time GitHub contributor—directly in the Issues list view, making it instantly clear who is opening issues. This eliminates the need to open individual issues or check author profiles, saving time during triage and helping maintainers provide more targeted feedback to newcomers and established contributors alike.

Expected Outcome

We want to help maintainers make faster, better-informed triage and moderation decisions by surfacing contributor context directly where they need it. By bringing repository member role information to Issues lists—matching the experience already available in pull request lists—maintainers have context on who each Issue is coming from so they can triage more effectively.

entry.title: Private (personal) saved views [GA]
entry.content:
Value Prop

You can now save private views on any repository you can read — no triage access required. Private views are visible only to you, so you can keep personal filters separate from the shared views your whole team sees. Shared and private views appear together in the sidebar, making it easy to switch between your own workflow and the team's common view.

Expected Outcome

Saved views previously required triage access, which left most contributors — readers and collaborators — unable to save filters at all. Private views open this capability to everyone, mirroring the personal filter model already available on the global issues and pull requests pages, and give triage-level users a way to maintain working views without affecting their team's shared set.

entry.title: Focused issue timeline and activity panel [Public Preview]
entry.content:
Value Prop

Navigate and filter issue activity more efficiently with the new Activity panel. Instead of scrolling through a cluttered timeline and repeatedly clicking "Load more," you can now focus on the events and comments that matter to you, making it easier to follow conversations and find important context on any issue.

Expected Outcome

Issues become more navigable and performant by separating comments from the broader activity timeline. Users spend less time loading and parsing irrelevant events, and more time understanding the discussions that drive their work forward.

Hi Community! 👋

We want to take a moment to sincerely thank everyone who has participated in the discussions here in the past month. Your comments have been heard and appreciated, and they’ve played a meaningful role in shaping our conversations with our community and products.

To better serve our community and centralize discussions for our product team, we’ve disabled the ability to post on the GitHub Roadmap discussion board. Join us as we continue the conversation in the Community discussions!

The Community discussions are the ideal place to raise feature requests, share feedback, and connect with fellow members. With a dedicated team of community managers and active product managers closely monitoring the forums, this platform ensures better engagement and quicker responses compared to the roadmap discussions.

What’s next?

We have reviewed any user created Discussions and guided to the Community discussions where applicable. We will disable the ability for non GitHub staff to post on GitHub roadmap discussion boards.

Then we will update some roadmap issues with direct links to dedicated feedback discussions where we would love you to upvote and share your feedback where it fits best. Feel free to create a new discussion if needed!

We look forward to hearing your thoughts and engaging with you in the community discussions - see you there!👋
